# depsgx

> Inspect a module dependency graph for cycles, layer violations and dead code. Reports problems with stable codes and exit codes, and writes an annotated storyboard.

depsgx is one of the `gxkit` agent-native review tools. Declare modules and what
they depend on; `depsgx inspect` proves the graph is acyclic, that no dependency
points upward through the layers, and that nothing is unreachable from the entry
points.

## Install

```sh
uvx --from "git+https://github.com/nekomario28/gxkit#subdirectory=packages/depsgx" depsgx --help
uv tool install ./packages/depsgx      # from a clone
```

Needs Python 3.10+ and Pillow.

## Use

```sh
depsgx inspect deps.py            # report + storyboard, exit 1 on any error
depsgx inspect deps.py --json
depsgx inspect deps.py --no-storyboard
depsgx render  deps.py -o deps.png
```

A graph file defines `graph` (a `ModuleGraph`) or module-level `MODULES` /
`DEPENDS` / `ROOTS` / `FORBIDDEN` / `LAYERS`. `depends` points from a module to
what it imports.

## Checks

error: `cycle`, `layer-violation`, `forbidden-dependency`, `self-dependency`,
`dangling-dependency`, `dangling-reference` (a `forbidden` pair, layer member or
root that names no module).
info: `unreachable-module`, `orphan-module`, `duplicate-dependency`, `no-roots`.

Full documentation is in `README.md`.
